key_terms.meaning: One binary digit, a 0 or a 1; the smallest unit of digital information.
1's complement plus 1; the standard code for negative binary numbers, and subtraction becomes addition.
Binary-coded decimal: each decimal digit 0–9 is stored as its own 4-bit binary group.
A gate type, NAND or NOR, from which every other gate and every Boolean function can be built.
A product term containing every variable once, equal to 1 in exactly one row of the truth table.
A sum term containing every variable once, equal to 0 in exactly one row of the truth table.
A grid of truth-table cells laid out in Gray-code order so that neighbouring cells differ in one variable only.
An input combination whose output is irrelevant; written X and treated as 0 or 1 to make larger groups.
A combinational circuit that adds three bits A, B and carry-in Cin to give sum S and carry-out Cout.
A selector with 2ⁿ data inputs, n select lines and one output; the output copies the selected input.
A router that sends one input to one of 2ⁿ outputs chosen by n select lines.
A bistable circuit that stores one bit because its output is fed back to its own input.
Clocking in which a flip-flop changes state only at the rising or falling edge of the clock pulse.
Arithmetic Logic Unit: the CPU block that performs add, subtract, AND, OR, compare and shift operations.
The CPU block that decodes each instruction and issues the timing and control signals for the other blocks.
A one-way bus carrying the address of the memory location or port the CPU wants to reach.
A bidirectional bus carrying the actual data bytes between the CPU, memory and input/output devices.
General Purpose Input/Output: a microcontroller pin whose direction and function the program sets at run time.
Analog-to-digital converter: changes a measured voltage into a binary code the processor can read.
A design with separate buses for program memory and data memory, so an instruction and its data can be fetched together.

takeaways: One pattern of bits can be read as unsigned binary, 2's complement, octal, hexadecimal or BCD; the reading rule fixes the value.
Subtraction is done as 2's complement addition, so a single adder circuit handles both operations.
NAND alone, or NOR alone, can build NOT, AND, OR and therefore every logic circuit.
A truth table has exactly one canonical SOP form and one canonical POS form; K-map grouping removes the variables that change inside a group.
A half adder is just the truth table of one-column binary addition, and cascading full adders gives multi-bit addition.
A multiplexer with n select lines can implement any n-variable Boolean function without any other gate.
A flip-flop stores a bit only because its output feeds its input, so feedback is the basis of all digital memory.
A microcontroller is a CPU with program memory, data memory, timers and GPIO pins on one chip, built to control a device.
Bus width decides how much memory a CPU can address and how fast data moves; the address bus is one-way, the data bus is two-way.
Harvard architecture and a reduced instruction set both raise speed at the cost of simpler, more predictable hardware.
bank_note: Long answers in this unit usually demand a full chain of work: truth table, then K-map or Boolean reduction, then a gate-level or multiplexer-level circuit with pin counts, and for the last chapter a labelled block diagram with each bus and block explained.

bank.q: Name the number systems used in digital systems and state, for each, its base, its digit set and its place weights.
outline: Binary base 2, digits 0–1, weights 2⁰, 2¹, 2², ...
Octal base 8, digits 0–7, weights powers of 8
Decimal base 10, digits 0–9, used only at the human interface
Hexadecimal base 16, digits 0–9 and A–F, weights powers of 16
One line each on why octal and hex are used: shorthand for 3 and 4 bits

bank.q: Explain 2's complement representation of signed binary numbers. Give the range for 8 bits and explain the steps for subtraction with an example.
outline: Definition: 2's complement of N = 1's complement + 1; sign bit is the MSB, 0 for positive and 1 for negative
Range for n bits: −2ⁿ⁻¹ to +2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, so −128 to +127 for 8 bits
Subtraction steps: take 2's complement of the subtrahend, add, discard the final carry
Worked example such as 45 − 68 giving a negative result in 2's complement
Advantages: single zero, no separate subtractor circuit, addition circuit reused

bank.q: State the basic Boolean identities and De Morgan's laws, and prove that NAND and NOR are universal gates.
outline: Identities: A + 0 = A, A·1 = A, A + A = A, A·A' = 0, A + A' = 1, absorption, distributive laws
De Morgan: (A·B)' = A' + B' and (A + B)' = A'·B', proved by truth table
NAND as NOT, AND, OR with gate diagrams
NOR as NOT, AND, OR with gate diagrams
Conclusion: any function in SOP form can be built from NAND alone; any POS function from NOR alone

bank.q: Define minterm and maxterm. For a 3-variable function F(A,B,C) give the truth table and write F in Σm and ΠM notation.
outline: Minterm definition with 3-variable example A'BC' = m₂
Maxterm definition with example (A + B' + C) = M₂
Identity mᵢ' = Mᵢ and Σm list versus ΠM list are complementary
Truth table with 8 rows and the decimal index of each row
Canonical SOP written as Σm(...) and canonical POS written as ΠM(...)

bank.q: Perform these conversions and show every step: (i) (1101.011)₂ to decimal and hexadecimal, (ii) (255)₁₀ to binary and octal, (iii) (743)₈ to hexadecimal through binary, (iv) (10110110)₂ as an 8-bit 2's complement decimal value.
outline: Positional expansion with weights for the fractional binary case
Grouping 4 bits from the binary point for hex, 3 bits for octal
Repeated division by 2 or 8 for the decimal to binary and octal parts
Octal to binary to hex route, regrouping from the right
Sign-bit check and 2's complement step for part (iv), giving −74

bank.q: Explain BCD addition with the correction rule. Add 47 and 38 in BCD and show where and why 0110 is added.
outline: Each decimal digit written as 4 bits; invalid codes 1010 to 1111 never used
Add nibble by nibble like binary
Correction: if a nibble sum exceeds 9 or a carry leaves the nibble, add 0110
Worked 47 + 38 = 85 with the carry into the next nibble
Reason: 16 is added by hardware but decimal needs 10, so 6 is added back

bank.q: Minimise a given 4-variable Boolean function with don't-care terms using a K-map by the SOP method, and repeat by the POS method. Compare the gate counts of both results.
outline: Correctly filled 16-cell map with Gray-code row and column labels
Groups of 1, 2, 4, 8, each a power of two, overlapping allowed, X used freely
SOP result read from groups of 1s; POS result read from groups of 0s using the complemented variable rule
Both answers checked against the original truth table
Gate count comparison: number of AND and OR inputs, inverters needed for POS

bank.q: Design a half adder and a full adder from truth table to K-map to gate circuit, then connect four full adders as a 4-bit ripple carry adder and explain its carry delay.
outline: Half adder: S = A ⊕ B, C = A·B, truth table and gate diagram
Full adder truth table with three inputs; K-map giving S = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin and Cout = AB + Cin(A ⊕ B)
Full adder built from two half adders and one OR gate
4-bit ripple carry adder block diagram with carry chained left
Delay: each carry passes two gate delays, so the worst-case delay grows with the number of bits

bank.q: Draw the block diagram of a BCD adder using a 4-bit binary adder and explain the correction logic. Verify with 8 + 7.
outline: 4-bit binary adder producing an interim sum and carry
Detection term = carry-out + S₃S₂ + S₃S₁, which flags a sum above 9
Second 4-bit adder that adds 0110 when the flag is 1
Worked 8 + 7 = 15 giving 0001 0101 in BCD
Note that a final carry-out becomes the next decimal digit

bank.q: Explain a 4×1 multiplexer and a 1×4 demultiplexer with block diagrams, truth tables and Boolean expressions. Then implement F(A,B,C) = Σm(1,2,4,7) using an 8×1 multiplexer.
outline: MUX: 4 data inputs, 2 select lines, output Y = S₁'S₀'D₀ + S₁'S₀D₁ + S₁S₀'D₂ + S₁S₀D₃
DEMUX: one input, 2 select lines, four outputs, each equation and truth table
MUX as a function generator: connect A, B, C to select lines and tie each data input to 0 or 1
Data inputs for the given function: D₁ = D₂ = D₄ = D₇ = 1, all others 0
One line on MUX trees for larger functions

bank.q: Explain the SR, JK, D and T flip-flops with logic diagrams, truth tables and characteristic equations. Explain the race-around problem in the JK flip-flop and how edge triggering removes it.
outline: SR latch built from cross-coupled NOR or NAND gates, with the invalid state
JK flip-flop truth table and Q(next) = JQ' + K'Q
D flip-flop Q(next) = D; T flip-flop Q(next) = T ⊕ Q
Race-around: when clock is high and J = K = 1 the output toggles repeatedly
Remedy: master-slave arrangement or edge-triggered clocking; mention setup and hold time

bank.q: Compare a microprocessor and a microcontroller on architecture, memory, buses, instruction set, cost, power and typical use. Draw the block diagram of an 8051-type microcontroller and explain the ALU, control unit, instruction register, program memory and GPIO ports.
outline: Microprocessor: CPU only, needs external RAM, ROM and I/O, wide address bus, high speed, general purpose computing
Microcontroller: CPU plus flash program memory, data RAM, timers, serial port and GPIO on one chip, low cost and low power, embedded control
Labelled block diagram: ALU, accumulator, control unit, IR, program counter, program memory, data memory, timers, ports
Role of the instruction register in holding the fetched opcode while it is decoded
Bus explanation: address bus one-way, data bus two-way, control bus carries read and write
Two or three applications such as washing machine control, water-level controller, motor speed control

bank.q: A room has three sensors and a lamp must glow when at least two sensors are active. Design the circuit, then compare three implementations: basic gates from the SOP form, NAND-only realisation, and a 4×1 multiplexer. State which you would choose for production and why.
outline: Truth table for the majority function with 8 rows
SOP from K-map: F = AB + BC + CA
NAND-only circuit drawn by double complementing the SOP expression
MUX implementation with two variables on the select lines and the third driving the data inputs
Comparison on gate count, IC packages needed, wiring effort and cost; recommendation with a reason

bank.q: Design a microcontroller-based overhead water-tank controller that switches a pump on when the tank is empty and off when it is full. Explain the role of the sensor, the ADC, the debouncing latch, the GPIO pins, the program memory and the relay driver.
outline: Block diagram: level sensor, signal conditioning, ADC, microcontroller, relay driver, pump, display
ADC resolution and the digital threshold values chosen for empty and full
GPIO pins configured as input for the sensor and output for the relay
Debouncing of the float switch and why a latch or flip-flop or software delay is used
Program stored in flash memory; program loop reads the input, compares and drives the output
Safety points: hysteresis band to stop rapid switching, relay isolation, fail-safe off state

glossary.def: A positional number system with base 2 in which each place value is a power of 2.
A base-8 system using digits 0 to 7, where one octal digit stands for exactly three bits.
A base-16 system using 0–9 and A–F, where one hex digit stands for exactly four bits.
The result of inverting every bit of a binary number.
The 1's complement plus 1, used to represent negative numbers and to turn subtraction into addition.
A decimal code in which each digit 0–9 is written as a separate 4-bit binary group.
A binary code in which consecutive values differ in exactly one bit, used for K-map labels and position encoders.
The algebra of two values 0 and 1 with the operations AND, OR and NOT, used to describe logic circuits.
A table listing every input combination of a logic function and the output for each.
A physical circuit with one output whose state is fixed by its input states according to one Boolean operation.
The pair of identities (A·B)' = A' + B' and (A + B)' = A'·B'.
A gate from which all other gates can be constructed; NAND and NOR have this property.
A product of all the variables of a function, each either complemented or not, that is 1 for exactly one input row.
A sum of all the variables of a function, each either complemented or not, that is 0 for exactly one input row.
A Boolean expression written as an OR of several AND terms.
A Boolean expression written as an AND of several OR terms.
A rectangular map of a truth table arranged so that adjacent cells differ in one variable, allowing visual minimisation.
An input combination that never occurs in practice, so its output may be chosen as 0 or 1 to simplify the circuit.
A circuit whose output depends only on the present inputs, with no memory of earlier inputs.
A circuit whose output depends on the present inputs and on the stored past state.
A periodic square wave that decides when a sequential circuit is allowed to change state.
A digital selector that connects one of several data inputs to a single output under the control of select lines.
A single chip containing a CPU, program memory, data memory, timers and input/output pins for controlling a device.
A general purpose input/output pin whose direction and logic level are set by the running program.
A group of parallel wires that carries addresses, data or control signals between the parts of a computer.
A circuit that converts a continuous analog voltage into a proportional binary number.
